bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Chinese competitive pressure — Chinese heavy engineering manufacturers, operating with large domestic capacities and economy-of-scale cost advantages, offer aggressive pricing across process equipment, boiler pressure parts and containers in both domestic and international markets. Intensifying global trade tensions may redirect Chinese output into third-party markets, amplifying competitive pressure in price-sensitive segments and geographies. Classified as a strategic risk; mitigated through quality certifications (ASME, PED, EN), delivery reliability, technology complexity and China+1 positioning with Western EPCs.
- Policy and regulatory risk narrowing addressable markets — The MoEF&CC notification of July 2025 restricted mandatory Flue Gas Desulphurisation installation to only certain categories of thermal power plants, materially reducing the addressable domestic FGD market. The emission control business is pivoting to Dry Sorbent Injection, Semi-Dry FGD, Electrostatic Precipitators, Bag Filters, Water Treatment and Balance of Plant, but full market development of these adjacencies will take time. Classified as a compliance risk.
- Commodity and input cost volatility — Alloy steel, nickel, industrial gases and fabrication steel are subject to global price cycles, logistics constraints and supply concentration. Although prices have moderated from H2 FY26 highs, global economic and geopolitical uncertainty may create periodic bouts of cost pressure that affect manufacturing margins, particularly in divisions with high alloy and specialty gas dependency. Mitigated by procurement on receipt of orders for key bought-outs, long-term vendor frameworks, alternative sourcing, fuel conversion initiatives, and for civil-work materials by rate contracts, back-to-back supplier offers, bulk purchases and global sourcing.
- Skilled manpower shortage constraining the capacity build-out — Constrained availability of skilled engineering and construction workforce is an execution risk precisely as the Company scales capacity across multiple divisions and enters new product lines and geographies, and is particularly relevant to the planned capacity expansions and new market entry initiatives in manufacturing. Revised labour laws could further constrain skilled-workforce availability at project sites. Permanent employee turnover was 14.32% and worker turnover 13.33% in FY 2025-26, with worker attrition roughly doubling from 7.5% in FY25.
- End-market demand moderation in sugar and ethanol after E20 — With India achieving its E20 blending target during 2025-26, new distillery investment is moderating as existing capacity is now in surplus relative to OMC ethanol allocations. Customer investment is shifting from basic capacity addition to high-efficiency modernisations and multi-feedstock flexibility, requiring the sugar and distillery business to pivot towards E30, SAF, CBG and advanced biofuels, exports and renewable energy to sustain growth.
- Domestic chlor-alkali overcapacity suppressing container demand — Structural overcapacity in India's chlor-alkali sector has suppressed domestic liquefied gas container demand, with major customers deferring procurement. Recovery depends on rationalisation of industry capacity, the timeline for which remains uncertain. Export markets are compensating but introduce greater logistics cost exposure.
- Concentration risk and rising export exposure — Flagged as a strategic risk in the Board's risk framework, mitigated through geographic diversification, new customer acquisition across divisions and sector diversification into defence, nuclear and green energy. No single customer individually accounted for more than 10% of revenue in the year ended March 31, 2026 (nil in the prior year), but exports rose to 22.36% of standalone turnover from roughly 10.6%, increasing exposure to international demand, freight and logistics costs; forex exposure is managed under a Foreign Exchange Risk Management Policy with all export and import exposures hedged with banks.
- Working capital and technology obsolescence in a long-cycle, licensor-dependent business — Working capital risk is classified as financial given the long-duration turnkey project business, mitigated through advance payments and milestone billing with working capital facilities managed centrally. Technology obsolescence is a strategic risk heightened by emerging and disruptive technologies and evolving customer preferences, mitigated through global technology partnerships, continuous manufacturing process innovation and digitisation investments across plants and embedded into products such as boilers and presses.

outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

outlook.body:
- Export-led growth: a deliberate strategic shift toward exports across multiple divisions, with international revenue rising from 14% of total in FY25 to roughly 22-23% in FY26, and management describing a progressively strengthening export market position entering FY27
- Position as a China+1 supplier to Western OEMs, EPC firms and end-customers, differentiating on quality certifications (ASME, PED, EN), delivery reliability and technology complexity as Western buyers diversify supply chains away from Chinese suppliers
- Diversify into defence, nuclear and green energy sectors, progressing defence-sector qualifications and positioning nuclear-grade Process Equipment and precision Contract Manufacturing (Calandria Vault Top Hatches, Beam & Deck Plate Assemblies, pressure vessels, shell & tube heat exchangers) for the Bharat Small Reactor / SMR opportunity
- Expand manufacturing capacity across multiple product lines - presses at Bhartoli, skids and modules at Dahej SEZ, iron and steel foundry machining at Bhartoli and Muzaffarnagar, boiler tubes and panels at Rattangarh - and pre-book orders so the new capacity is loaded on commissioning
- Move the product portfolio up the value chain into more sophisticated, higher value-added equipment and machines, and make small debottlenecking investments in plant and machinery across all other product lines to raise throughput and productivity
- Maintain a multi-product, multi-sector portfolio as a deliberate natural hedge against cyclicity in any individual end-market
- Sustain and deepen strategic technology partnerships and licensing tie-ups with global engineering leaders (Sumitomo SHI FW, BHI FW, Amec Foster Wheeler/Wood, Fuel Tech, Babcock Power Environmental, Envirotherm, CB&I Lummus, TEi, NEM Energy, AP&T) as the mitigation for technology obsolescence and to expand the addressable market
- Pivot the emission control business towards Dry Sorbent Injection, Semi-Dry FGD, Electrostatic Precipitators, Bag Filters, Water Treatment and Balance of Plant after the July 2025 MoEF&CC notification narrowed the mandatory FGD market
- Pivot the sugar and distillery business from basic distillery capacity addition towards E30, Sustainable Aviation Fuel, Compressed Biogas, advanced biofuels, high-efficiency modernisations, multi-feedstock flexibility and export markets
- Reduce net debt and fund the manufacturing capex programme entirely from internal accruals
- Improve shop-floor productivity, reduce cycle time and remain cost competitive; digitisation investments across plants and embedded into products such as Boilers and Presses
- Build a future-ready talent pool through multi-channel talent acquisition, campus recruitment from premier engineering institutions, apprenticeships and Women Leadership initiatives to support scaling capacity
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Isgec is investing to expand manufacturing capacity across multiple product lines, funded entirely from internal accruals. Press manufacturing capacity is being expanded at a new location at Bhartoli, Haryana, about 25 km from the existing Yamunanagar plant: Phase I of the Machine Building Division there is targeted for September 30, 2026, with Phase II due partly by June 30, 2027 and the balance by March 31, 2028. A new shop for manufacturing skids and modules for process industries is being set up on the Company's plot in the Dahej Special Economic Zone, Gujarat, with Phase I targeted for September 2027 and Phase II for March 2028. Precision machining capacity is being added at both foundries: a machine shop for steel castings at Muzaffarnagar was completed on May 31, 2026, a machine shop for iron castings at the Bhartoli foundry (transitioning it to machined supply) is due in June 2027, and a further steel foundry capacity expansion at Muzaffarnagar is targeted for December 2027. In the Boiler Tubes and Panels Division, construction of a new Preparation Shop and Coil Shop at Rattangarh works is complete with production expected to start by August 2026. Capacity expansions at the Piping Division and at the Standard Mechanical Presses plant at Bawal are already complete. In addition, a number of small capital investments in plant and machinery are being made across all other manufactured product lines to reduce bottlenecks and increase throughput and productivity. Management anticipates manufacturing revenue to grow progressively and significantly as these capacities are commissioned, and states it has already started booking new orders to load them immediately on commissioning; it is evaluating further investments to increase capacity for other manufactured products. The Company's twelve facilities together encompass more than 2,00,000 square metres of covered manufacturing area, with the Dahej SEZ process equipment plant and the Bhartoli machine building and castings plant both described as under construction.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects strong growth momentum across nearly all end-markets served by the Company over the next five to seven years, driven by sustained government capital expenditure, Make in India, import substitution and the China+1 diversification strategy of global companies
- Management anticipates manufacturing revenue to progressively grow significantly as the new production capacities are commissioned, and has already started booking orders to load them
- The manufacturing segment saw strong demand from domestic economic growth and investment across sectors as well as export markets, particularly for presses and alloy steel castings; good export orders were booked for press lines into South-East Asia and for steel castings
- Management expects good demand for the skids & modules product line for supply of sophisticated, large-sized, heavy modules for process industries, and expects demand for its products to be strong, with further capacity investments under evaluation
- Both foundry units delivered strong performance driven by consistent demand for high-quality alloy castings; the Muzaffarnagar foundry exported 40% of its total output
- Government capital expenditure of Rs 12.2 Lakh Crore budgeted for FY27 (+10.9%) is described as direct demand stimulus across infrastructure, power and industrial sectors that are the primary drivers of Isgec's order inflows
- Union Budget FY27 defence allocation of Rs 7.85 Lakh Crore (+15.2%) and defence capital expenditure of Rs 2.19 Lakh Crore (+21.8%) expand the addressable market for Isgec's emerging defence-sector qualifications
- Thermal power build-out is described as, by volume, the single largest addressable opportunity for Indian heavy engineering manufacturers supplying boiler pressure parts, turbine castings, emission control systems and material handling solutions; the Government proposes to add a minimum of 80 GW of new coal-based capacity by 2031-32
- Nuclear power is at an inflection point with 8 reactors under construction, 10 more in pre-project stages, 22.38 GW projected by 2031-32 and private participation enabled through Bharat Small Reactors and Bharat Small Modular Reactors - a new market for nuclear-grade precision engineering
- Hydro capacity targeted at 67 GW by 2031-32 plus 55 GW of Pumped Storage Projects, driving long-term demand for turbine casings, pump casings, butterfly valve castings and specialised structural castings that Isgec supplies as contract manufacturing
- The National Green Hydrogen Mission (Rs 19,744 Crore outlay, 5 MMT capacity target by 2030) is generating a direct and growing demand pipeline for process plant equipment, pressure vessels, heat exchangers, reactors and piping across Isgec's Process Equipment and Boiler divisions, reinforcing the forward order book
- The renewable shift is creating new demand for biomass boilers, waste-to-energy systems, waste heat recovery equipment and process plant equipment for green ammonia, green hydrogen and Compressed Biogas infrastructure
- The active Indian refinery expansion cycle (Barmer, Gujarat Refinery expansion, Numaligarh tripling; total refining capacity projected at ~309.5 MMTPA by 2028) generates sustained demand for heat exchangers, pressure vessels, reactors, columns and piping
- Cement industry capex of approximately Rs 1,20,000 Crore planned by top producers between FY26 and FY28, nearly 50% higher than the prior three years, with a growing focus on waste heat recovery, alternative fuels and carbon capture, addressed by Isgec's waste heat boilers, HRSGs, bag filters and steel castings
- Fertiliser sector self-reliance and the PLI scheme, plus coal-gasification and LNG feedstock diversification, represent sustained capital investment opportunities for the process plant equipment business, though timing of investment decisions is variable
- Record Indian port cargo throughput (915.17 Million Tonnes in 2025-26) and Sagarmala 2.0 support demand for bulk material handling systems, stacker reclaimers, cranes and ship loaders/unloaders
- Cumulative RBI rate reductions of 125 bps during FY26, with the repo held at 5.25%, have materially reduced financing costs for Isgec's industrial customers across capital goods, energy and infrastructure
- Structural tailwinds cited as firmly in place: the India growth story, China+1 sourcing shift, rising global defence spending and the sustained energy transition investment cycle; management describes itself as cautiously optimistic
- Demand dynamics in sugar/ethanol are shifting from basic capacity addition to high-efficiency modernisations, multi-feedstock flexibility and clean energy integration now that E20 is met and distillery capacity is in surplus relative to OMC allocations
- Wars in East Europe and West Asia had a marginal effect on the business
- Standalone order bookings during FY26 aggregated to Rs 5,56,100 Lakh, an increase of 9% over the previous financial year
- Consolidated order bookings during FY26 aggregated to Rs 6,53,300 Lakh, an increase of 13% over the previous financial year
- A robust order book is cited alongside steady dividends and a strong credit rating as evidence of balance-sheet strength; management describes the order book as strengthening as the business expands
- Good export orders were booked during the year, particularly for press lines for export customers in South-East Asia and for steel castings
- New orders have already been booked to load the incoming expansion capacities immediately on commissioning
- The National Green Hydrogen Mission is described as reinforcing the long-term relevance of the Company's forward order book

deepdive.thesis: Diversified heavy-engineering player split into a steady, high-margin **Manufacturing** business (12–13% EBIT, 3 yrs running) and a lower-margin, lumpier **Projects/EPC** business (4.58% EBIT FY26, guided to ~5.5% FY27). FY26 standalone was soft (rev +4.2%, below own 7–8% guide) but Q4 recovered hard (rev +16%, PBT +48% YoY). The big structural positives: **exports doubled to INR1,169 cr (22% of rev)** with rising market share, net debt halved, and order book healthy at ~INR7,000 cr opening FY27. The big overhang: the **Philippines ethanol asset (CBPI)** — reclassified from "held for sale" to continuing operations, dragging consolidated PAT down 25% via a INR104 cr depreciation catch-up and forex noise, though now operationally cash-positive. FY27 standalone growth guided 10–12%, led by manufacturing.

risks.note: Chinese heavy engineering manufacturers, operating with large domestic capacities and economy-of-scale cost advantages, offer aggressive pricing across process equipment, boiler pressure parts and containers in both domestic and international markets. Intensifying global trade tensions may redirect Chinese output into third-party markets, amplifying competitive pressure in price-sensitive segments and geographies. Classified as a strategic risk; mitigated through quality certifications (ASME, PED, EN), delivery reliability, technology complexity and China+1 positioning with Western EPCs.

The MoEF&CC notification of July 2025 restricted mandatory Flue Gas Desulphurisation installation to only certain categories of thermal power plants, materially reducing the addressable domestic FGD market. The emission control business is pivoting to Dry Sorbent Injection, Semi-Dry FGD, Electrostatic Precipitators, Bag Filters, Water Treatment and Balance of Plant, but full market development of these adjacencies will take time. Classified as a compliance risk.
risks.risk: Policy and regulatory risk narrowing addressable markets

risks.note: Alloy steel, nickel, industrial gases and fabrication steel are subject to global price cycles, logistics constraints and supply concentration. Although prices have moderated from H2 FY26 highs, global economic and geopolitical uncertainty may create periodic bouts of cost pressure that affect manufacturing margins, particularly in divisions with high alloy and specialty gas dependency. Mitigated by procurement on receipt of orders for key bought-outs, long-term vendor frameworks, alternative sourcing, fuel conversion initiatives, and for civil-work materials by rate contracts, back-to-back supplier offers, bulk purchases and global sourcing.

Constrained availability of skilled engineering and construction workforce is an execution risk precisely as the Company scales capacity across multiple divisions and enters new product lines and geographies, and is particularly relevant to the planned capacity expansions and new market entry initiatives in manufacturing. Revised labour laws could further constrain skilled-workforce availability at project sites. Permanent employee turnover was 14.32% and worker turnover 13.33% in FY 2025-26, with worker attrition roughly doubling from 7.5% in FY25.
risks.risk: Skilled manpower shortage constraining the capacity build-out

risks.note: With India achieving its E20 blending target during 2025-26, new distillery investment is moderating as existing capacity is now in surplus relative to OMC ethanol allocations. risks.note: Structural overcapacity in India's chlor-alkali sector has suppressed domestic liquefied gas container demand, with major customers deferring procurement. currentContext.expansion: Isgec is investing to expand manufacturing capacity across multiple product lines, funded entirely from internal accruals. Press manufacturing capacity is being expanded at a new location at Bhartoli, Haryana, about 25 km from the existing Yamunanagar plant: Phase I of the Machine Building Division there is targeted for September 30, 2026, with Phase II due partly by June 30, 2027 and the balance by March 31, 2028. A new shop for manufacturing skids and modules for process industries is being set up on the Company's plot in the Dahej Special Economic Zone, Gujarat, with Phase I targeted for September 2027 and Phase II for March 2028. Precision machining capacity is being added at both foundries: a machine shop for steel castings at Muzaffarnagar was completed on May 31, 2026, a machine shop for iron castings at the Bhartoli foundry (transitioning it to machined supply) is due in June 2027, and a further steel foundry capacity expansion at Muzaffarnagar is targeted for December 2027. In the Boiler Tubes and Panels Division, construction of a new Preparation Shop and Coil Shop at Rattangarh works is complete with production expected to start by August 2026. Capacity expansions at the Piping Division and at the Standard Mechanical Presses plant at Bawal are already complete. In addition, a number of small capital investments in plant and machinery are being made across all other manufactured product lines to reduce bottlenecks and increase throughput and productivity. Management anticipates manufacturing revenue to grow progressively and significantly as these capacities are commissioned, and states it has already started booking new orders to load them immediately on commissioning; it is evaluating further investments to increase capacity for other manufactured products. The Company's twelve facilities together encompass more than 2,00,000 square metres of covered manufacturing area, with the Dahej SEZ process equipment plant and the Bhartoli machine building and castings plant both described as under construction.

risks.note: Chinese heavy engineering manufacturers, operating with large domestic capacities and economy-of-scale cost advantages, offer aggressive pricing across process equipment, boiler pressure parts and containers in both domestic and international markets. Intensifying global trade tensions may redirect Chinese output into third-party markets, amplifying competitive pressure in price-sensitive segments and geographies. Classified as a strategic risk; mitigated through quality certifications (ASME, PED, EN), delivery reliability, technology complexity and China+1 positioning with Western EPCs.

risks.risk: Policy and regulatory risk narrowing addressable markets
risks.note: The MoEF&CC notification of July 2025 restricted mandatory Flue Gas Desulphurisation installation to only certain categories of thermal power plants, materially reducing the addressable domestic FGD market. The emission control business is pivoting to Dry Sorbent Injection, Semi-Dry FGD, Electrostatic Precipitators, Bag Filters, Water Treatment and Balance of Plant, but full market development of these adjacencies will take time. Classified as a compliance risk.

Alloy steel, nickel, industrial gases and fabrication steel are subject to global price cycles, logistics constraints and supply concentration. Although prices have moderated from H2 FY26 highs, global economic and geopolitical uncertainty may create periodic bouts of cost pressure that affect manufacturing margins, particularly in divisions with high alloy and specialty gas dependency. Mitigated by procurement on receipt of orders for key bought-outs, long-term vendor frameworks, alternative sourcing, fuel conversion initiatives, and for civil-work materials by rate contracts, back-to-back supplier offers, bulk purchases and global sourcing.

risks.risk: Skilled manpower shortage constraining the capacity build-out
risks.note: Constrained availability of skilled engineering and construction workforce is an execution risk precisely as the Company scales capacity across multiple divisions and enters new product lines and geographies, and is particularly relevant to the planned capacity expansions and new market entry initiatives in manufacturing. Revised labour laws could further constrain skilled-workforce availability at project sites. Permanent employee turnover was 14.32% and worker turnover 13.33% in FY 2025-26, with worker attrition roughly doubling from 7.5% in FY25.

risks.risk: End-market demand moderation in sugar and ethanol after E20
risks.note: With India achieving its E20 blending target during 2025-26, new distillery investment is moderating as existing capacity is now in surplus relative to OMC ethanol allocations. Customer investment is shifting from basic capacity addition to high-efficiency modernisations and multi-feedstock flexibility, requiring the sugar and distillery business to pivot towards E30, SAF, CBG and advanced biofuels, exports and renewable energy to sustain growth.

risks.risk: Domestic chlor-alkali overcapacity suppressing container demand
risks.note: Structural overcapacity in India's chlor-alkali sector has suppressed domestic liquefied gas container demand, with major customers deferring procurement. Recovery depends on rationalisation of industry capacity, the timeline for which remains uncertain. Export markets are compensating but introduce greater logistics cost exposure.

risks.risk: Concentration risk and rising export exposure
risks.note: Flagged as a strategic risk in the Board's risk framework, mitigated through geographic diversification, new customer acquisition across divisions and sector diversification into defence, nuclear and green energy. No single customer individually accounted for more than 10% of revenue in the year ended March 31, 2026 (nil in the prior year), but exports rose to 22.36% of standalone turnover from roughly 10.6%, increasing exposure to international demand, freight and logistics costs; forex exposure is managed under a Foreign Exchange Risk Management Policy with all export and import exposures hedged with banks.

risks.risk: Working capital and technology obsolescence in a long-cycle, licensor-dependent business
risks.note: Working capital risk is classified as financial given the long-duration turnkey project business, mitigated through advance payments and milestone billing with working capital facilities managed centrally. Technology obsolescence is a strategic risk heightened by emerging and disruptive technologies and evolving customer preferences, mitigated through global technology partnerships, continuous manufacturing process innovation and digitisation investments across plants and embedded into products such as boilers and presses.

thesis: Diversified heavy-engineering player split into a steady, high-margin **Manufacturing** business (12–13% EBIT, 3 yrs running) and a lower-margin, lumpier **Projects/EPC** business (4.58% EBIT FY26, guided to ~5.5% FY27). FY26 standalone was soft (rev +4.2%, below own 7–8% guide) but Q4 recovered hard (rev +16%, PBT +48% YoY). The big structural positives: **exports doubled to INR1,169 cr (22% of rev)** with rising market share, net debt halved, and order book healthy at ~INR7,000 cr opening FY27. The big overhang: the **Philippines ethanol asset (CBPI)** — reclassified from "held for sale" to continuing operations, dragging consolidated PAT down 25% via a INR104 cr depreciation catch-up and forex noise, though now operationally cash-positive. FY27 standalone growth guided 10–12%, led by manufacturing.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Isgec Heavy Engineering is a diversified Indian heavy-engineering conglomerate founded in 1933, supplying capital goods, turnkey industrial projects and sugar & ethanol, with equipment supplied across 99 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Isgec designs, manufactures and executes engineering solutions across three segments: manufacturing of machinery and equipment (presses, process plant equipment such as reactors, pressure vessels, heat exchangers and columns, boiler pressure parts and piping spools, liquefied gas containers, iron and steel castings, and contract manufacturing), industrial projects (industrial and green-energy boilers, sugar plants and distilleries, emission control systems, bulk material handling, railway and metro projects, wastewater treatment and process plants on a single-point turnkey basis), and sugar and ethanol through wholly owned subsidiary Saraswati Sugar Mills. It serves customer industries including power generation, oil and gas, petrochemicals, automotive, fertilisers, green energy, hydro power, mining, paper, sugar, steel, cement, chemicals, railways, distilleries, aerospace and port infrastructure, in India and internationally. The Company operates nine manufacturing facilities in India plus one in Canada and a step-down ethanol plant in the Philippines, and is listed on the BSE and NSE.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:

- Management anticipates manufacturing revenue to progressively grow significantly as the new production capacities are commissioned, and has already started booking orders to load them
- The manufacturing segment saw strong demand from domestic economic growth and investment across sectors as well as export markets, particularly for presses and alloy steel castings; good export orders were booked for press lines into South-East Asia and for steel castings
- Management expects good demand for the skids & modules product line for supply of sophisticated, large-sized, heavy modules for process industries, and expects demand for its products to be strong, with further capacity investments under evaluation
- Both foundry units delivered strong performance driven by consistent demand for high-quality alloy castings; the Muzaffarnagar foundry exported 40% of its total output
- Government capital expenditure of Rs 12.2 Lakh Crore budgeted for FY27 (+10.9%) is described as direct demand stimulus across infrastructure, power and industrial sectors that are the primary drivers of Isgec's order inflows
- Union Budget FY27 defence allocation of Rs 7.85 Lakh Crore (+15.2%) and defence capital expenditure of Rs 2.19 Lakh Crore (+21.8%) expand the addressable market for Isgec's emerging defence-sector qualifications
- Thermal power build-out is described as, by volume, the single largest addressable opportunity for Indian heavy engineering manufacturers supplying boiler pressure parts, turbine castings, emission control systems and material handling solutions; the Government proposes to add a minimum of 80 GW of new coal-based capacity by 2031-32
- Nuclear power is at an inflection point with 8 reactors under construction, 10 more in pre-project stages, 22.38 GW projected by 2031-32 and private participation enabled through Bharat Small Reactors and Bharat Small Modular Reactors - a new market for nuclear-grade precision engineering
- Hydro capacity targeted at 67 GW by 2031-32 plus 55 GW of Pumped Storage Projects, driving long-term demand for turbine casings, pump casings, butterfly valve castings and specialised structural castings that Isgec supplies as contract manufacturing
- The National Green Hydrogen Mission (Rs 19,744 Crore outlay, 5 MMT capacity target by 2030) is generating a direct and growing demand pipeline for process plant equipment, pressure vessels, heat exchangers, reactors and piping across Isgec's Process Equipment and Boiler divisions, reinforcing the forward order book
- The renewable shift is creating new demand for biomass boilers, waste-to-energy systems, waste heat recovery equipment and process plant equipment for green ammonia, green hydrogen and Compressed Biogas infrastructure
- The active Indian refinery expansion cycle (Barmer, Gujarat Refinery expansion, Numaligarh tripling; total refining capacity projected at ~309.5 MMTPA by 2028) generates sustained demand for heat exchangers, pressure vessels, reactors, columns and piping
- Cement industry capex of approximately Rs 1,20,000 Crore planned by top producers between FY26 and FY28, nearly 50% higher than the prior three years, with a growing focus on waste heat recovery, alternative fuels and carbon capture, addressed by Isgec's waste heat boilers, HRSGs, bag filters and steel castings
- Fertiliser sector self-reliance and the PLI scheme, plus coal-gasification and LNG feedstock diversification, represent sustained capital investment opportunities for the process plant equipment business, though timing of investment decisions is variable
- Record Indian port cargo throughput (915.17 Million Tonnes in 2025-26) and Sagarmala 2.0 support demand for bulk material handling systems, stacker reclaimers, cranes and ship loaders/unloaders
- Cumulative RBI rate reductions of 125 bps during FY26, with the repo held at 5.25%, have materially reduced financing costs for Isgec's industrial customers across capital goods, energy and infrastructure
- Structural tailwinds cited as firmly in place: the India growth story, China+1 sourcing shift, rising global defence spending and the sustained energy transition investment cycle; management describes itself as cautiously optimistic
- Demand dynamics in sugar/ethanol are shifting from basic capacity addition to high-efficiency modernisations, multi-feedstock flexibility and clean energy integration now that E20 is met and distillery capacity is in surplus relative to OMC allocations
- Wars in East Europe and West Asia had a marginal effect on the business
- Standalone order bookings during FY26 aggregated to Rs 5,56,100 Lakh, an increase of 9% over the previous financial year
- Consolidated order bookings during FY26 aggregated to Rs 6,53,300 Lakh, an increase of 13% over the previous financial year
- A robust order book is cited alongside steady dividends and a strong credit rating as evidence of balance-sheet strength; management describes the order book as strengthening as the business expands
- Good export orders were booked during the year, particularly for press lines for export customers in South-East Asia and for steel castings
- New orders have already been booked to load the incoming expansion capacities immediately on commissioning
- The National Green Hydrogen Mission is described as reinforcing the long-term relevance of the Company's forward order book

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Isgec is investing to expand manufacturing capacity across multiple product lines, funded entirely from internal accruals. Press manufacturing capacity is being expanded at a new location at Bhartoli, Haryana, about 25 km from the existing Yamunanagar plant: Phase I of the Machine Building Division there is targeted for September 30, 2026, with Phase II due partly by June 30, 2027 and the balance by March 31, 2028. A new shop for manufacturing skids and modules for process industries is being set up on the Company's plot in the Dahej Special Economic Zone, Gujarat, with Phase I targeted for September 2027 and Phase II for March 2028. Precision machining capacity is being added at both foundries: a machine shop for steel castings at Muzaffarnagar was completed on May 31, 2026, a machine shop for iron castings at the Bhartoli foundry (transitioning it to machined supply) is due in June 2027, and a further steel foundry capacity expansion at Muzaffarnagar is targeted for December 2027. In the Boiler Tubes and Panels Division, construction of a new Preparation Shop and Coil Shop at Rattangarh works is complete with production expected to start by August 2026. Capacity expansions at the Piping Division and at the Standard Mechanical Presses plant at Bawal are already complete. In addition, a number of small capital investments in plant and machinery are being made across all other manufactured product lines to reduce bottlenecks and increase throughput and productivity. Management anticipates manufacturing revenue to grow progressively and significantly as these capacities are commissioned, and states it has already started booking new orders to load them immediately on commissioning; it is evaluating further investments to increase capacity for other manufactured products. The Company's twelve facilities together encompass more than 2,00,000 square metres of covered manufacturing area, with the Dahej SEZ process equipment plant and the Bhartoli machine building and castings plant both described as under construction.

thesis: Diversified heavy-engineering player split into a steady, high-margin **Manufacturing** business (12–13% EBIT, 3 yrs running) and a lower-margin, lumpier **Projects/EPC** business (4.58% EBIT FY26, guided to ~5.5% FY27). FY26 standalone was soft (rev +4.2%, below own 7–8% guide) but Q4 recovered hard (rev +16%, PBT +48% YoY). The big structural positives: **exports doubled to INR1,169 cr (22% of rev)** with rising market share, net debt halved, and order book healthy at ~INR7,000 cr opening FY27. The big overhang: the **Philippines ethanol asset (CBPI)** — reclassified from "held for sale" to continuing operations, dragging consolidated PAT down 25% via a INR104 cr depreciation catch-up and forex noise, though now operationally cash-positive. FY27 standalone growth guided 10–12%, led by manufacturing.

|---|---|---|
| **Standalone Revenue** | INR5,229 cr | +4.2% YoY (below own 7–8% guide); Q4 rev +16% YoY |
| **Standalone PBT (reported)** | INR455 cr | +17% YoY; Q4 PBT +48% YoY |
| **Standalone PBT (normalized)** | ~INR375 cr | Excl. ~INR80 cr Philippines-related items → broadly flat YoY operationally |
| **Mfg EBIT margin** | 12.46% | Within 12–13% guided band (3 yrs running) |
| **Projects/EPC EBIT margin** | 4.58% | Guided to ~5.5% in FY27 |
| **Export revenue** | INR1,169 cr (~22% of rev) | Up from INR532 cr (~14%) — more than doubled YoY |
| **Consol EBITDA** | INR671 cr | +19% YoY (vs INR566 cr) |
| **Consol PAT** | INR154 cr | −25% YoY (vs INR204 cr) — hit by Philippines depreciation catch-up |
| **Consol depreciation** | INR278 cr | +INR104 cr YoY (Philippines catch-up on reclassification) |
| **Consol Net borrowings** | INR476 cr | Down from INR836 cr — improved substantially |
| **Standalone cash & equiv** | INR241 cr (31-Mar-26) | After funding ~INR150 cr capex from internal accruals |
| **Capex (FY26)** | INR153 cr | Capacity additions across most mfg lines |
| **Dividend** | INR6/share | +20% YoY |

**One-offs / non-operational (FLAGGED):**
- ~INR80 cr of standalone PBT from Philippines-related items — real P&L but **not core operational earnings**; underlying operational PBT ~INR375 cr.
- Consol depreciation includes **INR104 cr YoY increase** = catch-up charge on Philippines (CBPI) assets reclassified from held-for-sale to continuing operations.
- CBPI full-year reported loss INR295 cr = INR170 cr depreciation + INR95 cr forex variation (nets off vs ISGEC) + ~INR70 cr interest accrual + ~INR26 cr genuine operational loss (plant ran only 3.5 months).
- Consol other income includes INR103 cr forex fluctuation gain; ~INR50 cr+ corresponding offset sits in other expenses (Isgec Investments Pte Ltd, Singapore) — gross-up per accounting standards.
- Other income parts: interest/net gain on current investments; government grants (Saraswati Sugar Mills); forex (Eagle Press + Singapore subsidiary).
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 standalone revenue: +10% to +12%.** Bulk from Manufacturing — ~INR500 cr / ~10% from mfg; Projects only ~3–4% growth.
- **Mfg EBIT margin: 12–13%** maintained (confident; back-to-back supplier orders + contingency margins hedge input-cost inflation).
- **Projects/EPC EBIT margin: ~5.5% in FY27** (up from 4.58%) — older orders completing, newer orders booked at better margins, shorter-gestation projects.
- **Order book:** opening FY27 ~INR7,000 cr (after excluding 2 cancelled orders worth ~INR550 cr). First 2 months of current quarter: new orders ~INR1,400 cr booked.
- **Mfg vs EPC mix:** growth tilted strongly to manufacturing.
- **Exports:** expect FY27 export revenue "a little more than" INR1,100–1,200 cr; export order book % to rise; weaker INR supports realizations.
- **Isgec Hitachi Zosen JV (FY27):** revenue ~INR700 cr, PBT INR100 cr+ (vs FY26 Total Income INR672 cr, PBT INR103 cr).
- **CBPI/Philippines (FY27):** plant running 70–75% now, targeting 85–90% utilization (ex ~1–1.5 months of heavy rain); cash-positive, self-sustaining, no further funding needed; depreciation ~INR150 cr (down from INR170 cr); no EBITDA number given.
order book & pipeline (segment split):
- **Opening FY27 order book: ~INR7,000 cr** (standalone, post excluding INR550 cr cancellations).
- **Export order book: ~INR1,450 cr** as on 31-Mar-2026 (expected to rise as % over FY27).
- **New orders booked Apr–May FY27: ~INR1,400 cr** (includes some export orders).
- **Isgec Hitachi Zosen orders in hand: INR763 cr** (31-Mar-2026); strong execution.
- **Cancellations:** 2 orders worth ~INR550 cr cancelled during FY26 (excluded from opening book).
- Inquiry pipeline "strong" in both domestic and export markets.
segment (manufacturing vs epc):
- **Manufacturing:** revenue booked on dispatch (sale-of-goods method) → quarter-to-quarter lumpy (Q3 strong, Q4 moderated purely on order/dispatch mix, not cost pressure). EBIT 12.46% FY26. New export markets for **presses in SE Asia** (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia). Steel castings expansion approved (Muzaffarnagar, +INR25 cr).
- **Projects/EPC:** EBIT 4.58% FY26; pivot (started ~1.5–2 yrs ago) from long-gestation to **shorter-gestation projects** is reducing working capital and execution risk → supports the ~5.5% FY27 margin. Geographies: developing countries — recent wins in **Africa and Latin America**.
growth / optionality:
- **Exports** as the structural growth engine — market-share gains in presses (SE Asia) and projects (Africa, LatAm); weaker INR a tailwind.
- **New-technology equipment plays:** ISGEC supplies equipment used in **coal gasification** and **polysilicon-to-wafer (solar)** value chains — already won equipment orders; "play in some part of the value chain."
- **Capacity additions coming online in FY27** to contribute to revenue.
- **CBPI ethanol** turning self-sustaining/cash-positive — optional value on eventual sale (running plant easier to sell).
- Diverse end-markets doing well: Sugar, Power, Oil & Gas, Automobiles, Fertilizers. Weak: paper; few new India ethanol plants.
margins & cost:
- Mfg 12–13% defended via back-to-back supplier orders placed soon after customer orders + contingency margins.
- **Input-cost inflation flagged:** steel forgings, castings, chemicals, certain imported materials; gas shortages raising fuel costs; longer/costlier export-import logistics. Most expected to be absorbed via normal contingency provisions.
- EPC margin lift driven by old-project completion + better-priced shorter new orders.
capex:
- FY26 capex INR153 cr (some references to ~INR150 cr), funded from internal accruals.
- Capacity additions across most manufacturing product lines — "on schedule with minor adjustments."
- **Board approved +INR25 cr** to expand Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant.
capital allocation:
- Net borrowings (consol) cut from INR836 cr → INR476 cr.
- Standalone: no working-capital borrowings; borrowings are on-lent to CBPI (shareholder-loan style funding of Philippines unit).
- Dividend INR6/share (+20% YoY).
- FGD retention money: >INR200 cr of the ~INR300 cr expected was realized; INR165 cr still outstanding (one-third expected in June, rest by August).
- Capex funded internally; cash & equiv INR241 cr at year-end.
risks (epc execution / margins):
- **Projects/EPC margin uncertainty** tied to geopolitical/war situation; mgmt "doesn't know when war will end."
- **Input-cost inflation** (steel, castings, forgings, imports, gas/fuel, logistics) — partially hedged, not fully eliminated.
- **Philippines/CBPI overhang:** no longer held-for-sale; sale timing uncertain (1–2 yrs hoped); prior deal collapsed (buyer couldn't fund). Depreciation/forex drag on consolidated PAT.
- **Subsidiary "capital deficiency"** (negative net worth) in Isgec Investments Pte Ltd & Bioeq Energy Holding — mgmt says immaterial as all borrowings are intra-group (shareholder loans).
- **Export receivables / FX risk** in Africa/LatAm — mitigated via confirmed LCs (USD/EUR), forward covers, and running cash-surplus payment schedules.
- Order cancellations (INR550 cr in FY26) show book is not immune.
mgmt tone: Transparent and measured. Proactively disclosed the INR80 cr non-operational PBT component and the underlying ~INR375 cr "true" PBT; candidly admitted FY26 missed its own 7–8% revenue guide; detailed the CBPI loss bridge line-by-line. Confident on manufacturing margins and exports; cautious/conditional on EPC margins and Philippines sale. Analysts praised the regular, detailed disclosure.
non-obvious:
- Manufacturing revenue is dispatch-based, so quarterly mfg margins/revenue are noise — **annual view required** (mgmt explicit).
- Reclassifying CBPI from "held for sale" to "continuing operations" is what mechanically crushed consol PAT (INR104 cr depreciation catch-up), not an operational deterioration.
- CBPI ethanol sales gated by **Philippine govt (Dept of Energy) allocations** per factory; allocations for Apr–Jun and Jul–Sep quarters → Q4 had almost no ethanol sales despite production (ethanol stocked). Already sold 4.35 million litres Apr–May FY27; contracts with ~6 Philippine oil companies (all blend/import, no refining).
- ~INR80 cr of standalone PBT is Philippines-related — flatters standalone optics.
- Forex gross-up (INR103 cr other income vs ~INR50 cr+ in other expenses) is presentation, not economic.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ **ISGEC itself** a beneficiary of: weaker INR (export realizations), post-COVID export push paying off (SE Asia presses, Africa/LatAm projects), and new-tech equipment demand (coal gasification, polysilicon-to-wafer/solar).
- ✅ Shorter-gestation EPC model → better working capital + margins.
